The main takeaway from our work is that
the cost of concurrency control is not always proportional to the number of conflicts, and the cost of atomicity is not necessarily proportional to the number or type of conflicts.
, under a relaxed isolation level, the overhead of concurrency control is negligible and the performance of distributed transactions can be comparable to that of single-item transactions.
, in a distributed environment, read-write and write-only transactions can be processed without synchronization and with low overhead, and thus can achieve very high performance.
